nodes.label: Next.js
nodes.description: Open-source full-stack web development framework for React-based web applications, supporting server-side and static rendering.

nodes.label: Vercel
nodes.description: Private company maintaining and leading open-source Next.js development and owning its copyright/trademarks.

nodes.label: React
nodes.description: JavaScript library traditionally used to build browser-rendered web applications.

nodes.label: Node.js
nodes.description: Runtime required by Next.js and used as the basis for server-rendered JavaScript applications.

nodes.label: JavaScript
nodes.description: Primary programming language used throughout the framework and its original design principles.

nodes.label: TypeScript
nodes.description: Language supported by Next.js and one of the languages in which Next.js itself is written.

nodes.label: Rust
nodes.description: Language used in major Next.js compiler/tooling components according to the supplied source.

nodes.label: Web platform
nodes.description: Platform identified for Next.js.

nodes.label: Full-stack web framework
nodes.description: Framework category covering both server and client/web application concerns.

nodes.label: MIT License
nodes.description: Open-source license identified for Next.js.

nodes.label: Server-side rendering
nodes.description: Rendering application content on the server before sending it to the client/browser.

nodes.label: Static rendering
nodes.description: Rendering/building content into static output that can be served without dynamic per-request rendering.

nodes.label: Client-side rendering
nodes.description: Traditional React model in which application content is rendered in the browser with JavaScript.

nodes.label: React Server Components
nodes.description: React component model supported by the App Router.

nodes.label: App Router
nodes.description: Next.js routing pattern introduced in beta in Next.js 13 and stabilized in 13.4.

nodes.label: Page-based routing
nodes.description: Next.js routing model described as a developer-convenience feature with dynamic routing support.

nodes.label: Dynamic routing
nodes.description: Routing support for dynamically determined paths.

nodes.label: Layouts
nodes.description: App Router capability for composing application layouts.

nodes.label: Streaming
nodes.description: App Router capability for streaming rendered content.

nodes.label: Data fetching
nodes.description: Configurable/data-fetching mechanisms provided by Next.js.

nodes.label: Automatic code splitting
nodes.description: Only code necessary to load a page is included, reducing browser loading burden.

nodes.label: Page prefetching
nodes.description: Prefetching intended to reduce load time.

nodes.label: Hot reloading
nodes.description: Detects changes and re-renders appropriate pages without requiring a server restart.

nodes.label: Hot-module replacement
nodes.description: Modules can be replaced live during development.

nodes.label: Deployment
nodes.description: Next.js emphasizes simplifying deployment and supports multiple deployment approaches.

nodes.label: npm
nodes.description: Terminal/package tool used to initialize and operate Next.js applications and its toolchain.

nodes.label: SWC
nodes.description: Open-source transpiler used by Next.js to transform and compile code into browser-usable JavaScript.

nodes.label: Webpack
nodes.description: Open-source module bundler used by Next.js, described as being replaced by Turbopack.

nodes.label: Turbopack
nodes.description: Bundler/tooling successor to Webpack, introduced in the Next.js tooling evolution.

nodes.label: Turborepo
nodes.description: Incremental build-system tool announced alongside the Turbo toolchain.

nodes.label: Turbo
nodes.description: Vercel front-end development toolchain containing Turbopack and Turborepo.

nodes.label: Rust compiler
nodes.description: Rust-based compiler introduced with Next.js 12 for faster compilation.

nodes.label: Edge Functions
nodes.description: Edge execution capability introduced in Next.js 12.

nodes.label: Middleware
nodes.description: Middleware capability introduced alongside Edge Functions in Next.js 12.

nodes.label: Native ESM
nodes.description: Native ECMAScript module support introduced in Next.js 12.

nodes.label: URL Imports
nodes.description: URL import support introduced in Next.js 12.

nodes.label: Sass
nodes.description: Precompiled Sass/SCSS styling supported by Next.js.

nodes.label: CSS
nodes.description: CSS styling supported by Next.js.

nodes.label: CSS Modules
nodes.description: CSS Modules supported by Next.js, with global CSS/CSS-module support noted in Next.js 9.3.

nodes.label: CSS-in-JS
nodes.description: CSS-in-JS styling approach supported by Next.js.

nodes.label: styled-jsx
nodes.description: Styling approach supported by Next.js.

nodes.label: AVIF
nodes.description: AVIF support introduced with Next.js 12.

nodes.label: Serverless deployment
nodes.description: Next.js 8 capability splitting application code into on-demand lambda functions.

nodes.label: Lambda function
nodes.description: On-demand function execution unit used by the described serverless deployment model.

nodes.label: Static export
nodes.description: Static-site export process improved in Next.js 8.

nodes.label: Incremental Static Regeneration
nodes.description: Next.js feature added in 9.5 allowing incremental regeneration of static content.

nodes.label: Rewrites
nodes.description: Request/URL rewrite capability added in Next.js 9.5.

nodes.label: Redirects
nodes.description: Redirect support added in Next.js 9.5.

nodes.label: Global Sass/CSS Modules
nodes.description: Global Sass and CSS Modules support introduced in Next.js 9.3.

nodes.label: React Context API
nodes.description: React Context API support for dynamic route handling was added in Next.js 7.

nodes.label: Webpack 4

nodes.label: Webpack 5
nodes.description: Webpack 5 support introduced in Next.js 11.

nodes.label: React 19
nodes.description: React 19 support introduced with Next.js 15 according to the source.

nodes.label: Asynchronous request APIs
nodes.description: Asynchronous request APIs introduced with Next.js 15.

nodes.label: Build Adapters API
nodes.description: Next.js 16 API enabling easier integration with hosting providers having custom requirements.

nodes.label: Self-deployment
nodes.description: Next.js has supported self-deployment since 2016 according to the source.

nodes.label: Next.js Live
nodes.description: Preview of real-time collaborative coding functionality introduced in Next.js 11.

nodes.label: Create React App Migration
nodes.description: Experimental Next.js 11 functionality for automatic conversion from Create React App.

nodes.description: Compilation/build process producing deployable application output.

nodes.description: Directory where the compiled website is usually saved during build time.

nodes.label: Pre-built static HTML
nodes.description: Static HTML pages produced during build time for static generation.

nodes.label: Cache
nodes.description: Cached pre-built static version served in response to requests.

nodes.label: Web browser
nodes.description: Client that receives rendered/static content and can execute browser-side JavaScript.

nodes.label: First-time visitor
nodes.description: Scenario where server-side rendering can reduce the burden before the browser has downloaded assets.

nodes.label: Site assets
nodes.description: JavaScript/CSS/other resources that the browser downloads for the application.

nodes.label: Search engine optimization
nodes.description: Site discoverability/optimization concern affected by rendering strategy.

nodes.label: Page load time
nodes.description: Time required to load/render content in the browser.

nodes.label: Browser workload
nodes.description: Client-side computational/loading burden that server rendering can reduce.

nodes.label: Rendering-related security benefit

nodes.label: Rendering choice
nodes.description: rendering_mode ∈ {client, server, static}
nodes.meaning: Next.js expands React's client-rendering model with server/static rendering.

nodes.label: Static delivery flow
nodes.description: source → build → .next → static HTML → cache → browser
nodes.expression: source → build → .next → static HTML → cache → browser
nodes.meaning: Build-time static generation produces artifacts that can be cached and served.

nodes.label: Automatic code splitting
nodes.description: page_request → required_code_only
nodes.meaning: Only code necessary to load a page is included.

nodes.label: Serverless execution
nodes.description: application_code → lambda_functions → on_demand_execution
nodes.meaning: Next.js 8 split code into on-demand lambda functions.

nodes.label: App Router architecture
nodes.description: route → layout + server_component + stream + data_fetching
nodes.meaning: App Router combines layouts, React Server Components, streaming and new data fetching.

nodes.label: Compilation toolchain
nodes.description: source → SWC/compiler → bundler → browser/deployment
nodes.meaning: Next.js uses compiler/transpiler and bundling stages.

nodes.label: Development update loop
nodes.description: code_change → detect → rerender/replace_module → browser
nodes.meaning: Hot reload/HMR provides immediate development feedback.

nodes.label: Incremental regeneration
nodes.description: static_output + later_regeneration
nodes.meaning: ISR extends static generation with incremental regeneration.

nodes.label: Routing
nodes.description: URL/path → routing_system → page/component
nodes.meaning: Next.js provides page-based and dynamic routing plus App Router.

nodes.label: Security update chain
nodes.description: vulnerability → CVE → affected_versions → fix_package → updated_version
nodes.meaning: Source describes a React vulnerability propagating downstream to Next.js and being fixed through an npm package.

nodes.label: Server-side vs client-side rendering
nodes.description: Server rendering occurs before content is sent to the browser; traditional React client rendering occurs in the browser.

nodes.label: Static vs dynamic rendering
nodes.description: Static output is built/cached ahead of requests; interactive/changing sites may not fit pure static generation.

nodes.label: SSR vs ISR
nodes.description: SSR renders on the server; ISR retains static output while supporting incremental regeneration.

nodes.label: App Router vs page-based routing
nodes.description: App Router is the newer routing architecture with layouts/RSC/streaming; page-based routing is the older routing model described by the source.

nodes.label: Webpack vs Turbopack
nodes.description: Webpack was the established bundler; Turbopack is described as its successor/replacement.

nodes.label: Compiler/transpiler vs bundler
nodes.description: SWC transforms/compiles code while Webpack/Turbopack bundle modules.

nodes.label: Code splitting vs prefetching
nodes.description: Code splitting reduces shipped code; prefetching anticipates resources to reduce load time.

nodes.label: Hot reload vs HMR
nodes.description: Both provide rapid development updates; HMR specifically replaces modules live.

nodes.label: Node/server vs browser runtime
nodes.description: Next.js spans server/runtime execution and browser delivery rather than being purely client-side.

nodes.label: Serverless vs self-deployment
nodes.description: Serverless uses on-demand functions; self-deployment is separately supported.

nodes.label: Next.js vs React
nodes.description: React is the underlying UI library; Next.js is a framework adding application architecture and rendering/deployment capabilities.

nodes.label: Edge runtime vs traditional server rendering
nodes.description: Edge capabilities are a deployment/runtime feature; server rendering is an application rendering model.

nodes.label: Framework vs toolchain
nodes.description: Next.js is the framework; Turbo/Turbopack/Turborepo are supporting development/build tools.

nodes.label: Vulnerability vs remediation
nodes.description: CVE records identify vulnerabilities; fix-react2shell-next is the remediation package described by the source.

nodes.label: Next.js is just React
nodes.description: Next.js is described as a full-stack framework built around React, adding server/static rendering, routing, data fetching, bundling and deployment capabilities.

nodes.label: Next.js only renders on the server
nodes.description: Next.js supports server rendering, static rendering, and client-side React behavior.

nodes.label: Static generation works for every site
nodes.description: The source explicitly notes static output is not suitable for every site, particularly highly interactive sites with frequent changes/user input.

nodes.label: SSR and static generation are identical
nodes.description: The source distinguishes server-side rendering from build-time static generation and caching.

nodes.label: App Router was always the Next.js routing system
nodes.description: App Router was introduced in Next.js 13 and stabilized in 13.4.

nodes.label: Turbopack and SWC do the same thing
nodes.description: SWC is described as a transpiler/compiler; Turbopack is a bundler.

nodes.label: Hot reload means the server must restart
nodes.description: Hot reloading is specifically described as avoiding server restart while reflecting code changes.

nodes.label: Next.js cannot deploy without Vercel
nodes.description: The source says Next.js has supported self-deployment since 2016 and Next.js 16 adds Build Adapters for hosting integration.

nodes.label: Next.js 13.4 only added another experimental router
nodes.description: The source says 13.4 made App Router stable for production.

nodes.label: Server rendering automatically makes every application secure
nodes.description: The source attributes an enhanced-security benefit to server rendering but separately documents a severe Next.js/React vulnerability.

nodes.label: Next.js versions have no architectural evolution
nodes.description: The source documents a progression from page routing/server rendering through App Router, RSC, streaming, Rust tooling and Build Adapters.

nodes.label: Webpack is the only bundler Next.js uses
nodes.description: The source describes Webpack and its replacement/evolution toward Turbopack.

semantic_distinctions.label: Server-side vs client-side rendering
semantic_distinctions.description: Server rendering occurs before content is sent to the browser; traditional React client rendering occurs in the browser.

semantic_distinctions.label: Static vs dynamic rendering
semantic_distinctions.description: Static output is built/cached ahead of requests; interactive/changing sites may not fit pure static generation.

semantic_distinctions.label: SSR vs ISR
semantic_distinctions.description: SSR renders on the server; ISR retains static output while supporting incremental regeneration.

semantic_distinctions.label: App Router vs page-based routing
semantic_distinctions.description: App Router is the newer routing architecture with layouts/RSC/streaming; page-based routing is the older routing model described by the source.

semantic_distinctions.label: Webpack vs Turbopack
semantic_distinctions.description: Webpack was the established bundler; Turbopack is described as its successor/replacement.

semantic_distinctions.label: Compiler/transpiler vs bundler
semantic_distinctions.description: SWC transforms/compiles code while Webpack/Turbopack bundle modules.

semantic_distinctions.label: Code splitting vs prefetching
semantic_distinctions.description: Code splitting reduces shipped code; prefetching anticipates resources to reduce load time.

semantic_distinctions.label: Hot reload vs HMR
semantic_distinctions.description: Both provide rapid development updates; HMR specifically replaces modules live.

semantic_distinctions.label: Node/server vs browser runtime
semantic_distinctions.description: Next.js spans server/runtime execution and browser delivery rather than being purely client-side.

semantic_distinctions.label: Serverless vs self-deployment
semantic_distinctions.description: Serverless uses on-demand functions; self-deployment is separately supported.

semantic_distinctions.label: Next.js vs React
semantic_distinctions.description: React is the underlying UI library; Next.js is a framework adding application architecture and rendering/deployment capabilities.

semantic_distinctions.label: Edge runtime vs traditional server rendering
semantic_distinctions.description: Edge capabilities are a deployment/runtime feature; server rendering is an application rendering model.

semantic_distinctions.label: Framework vs toolchain
semantic_distinctions.description: Next.js is the framework; Turbo/Turbopack/Turborepo are supporting development/build tools.

semantic_distinctions.label: Vulnerability vs remediation
semantic_distinctions.description: CVE records identify vulnerabilities; fix-react2shell-next is the remediation package described by the source.

misconceptions.label: Next.js is just React
misconceptions.description: Next.js is described as a full-stack framework built around React, adding server/static rendering, routing, data fetching, bundling and deployment capabilities.

misconceptions.label: Next.js only renders on the server
misconceptions.description: Next.js supports server rendering, static rendering, and client-side React behavior.

misconceptions.label: Static generation works for every site
misconceptions.description: The source explicitly notes static output is not suitable for every site, particularly highly interactive sites with frequent changes/user input.

misconceptions.label: SSR and static generation are identical
misconceptions.description: The source distinguishes server-side rendering from build-time static generation and caching.

misconceptions.label: App Router was always the Next.js routing system
misconceptions.description: App Router was introduced in Next.js 13 and stabilized in 13.4.

misconceptions.label: Turbopack and SWC do the same thing
misconceptions.description: SWC is described as a transpiler/compiler; Turbopack is a bundler.

misconceptions.label: Hot reload means the server must restart
misconceptions.description: Hot reloading is specifically described as avoiding server restart while reflecting code changes.

misconceptions.label: Next.js cannot deploy without Vercel
misconceptions.description: The source says Next.js has supported self-deployment since 2016 and Next.js 16 adds Build Adapters for hosting integration.

misconceptions.label: Next.js 13.4 only added another experimental router
misconceptions.description: The source says 13.4 made App Router stable for production.

misconceptions.label: Server rendering automatically makes every application secure
misconceptions.description: The source attributes an enhanced-security benefit to server rendering but separately documents a severe Next.js/React vulnerability.

misconceptions.label: Next.js versions have no architectural evolution
misconceptions.description: The source documents a progression from page routing/server rendering through App Router, RSC, streaming, Rust tooling and Build Adapters.

misconceptions.label: Webpack is the only bundler Next.js uses
misconceptions.description: The source describes Webpack and its replacement/evolution toward Turbopack.

historical_context.label: Initial release — 25 Oct 2016
historical_context.description: Next.js first released as an open-source GitHub project.

historical_context.label: Next.js 2.0 — March 2017
historical_context.description: Improvements for small websites, build efficiency and HMR scalability.

historical_context.label: Next.js 7 — September 2018
historical_context.description: Improved error handling, React Context API support, first Webpack 4 upgrade.

historical_context.label: Next.js 8 — February 2019
historical_context.description: First serverless deployment, improved static exports and prefetching.

historical_context.label: Next.js 9.3 — March 2020
historical_context.description: Optimizations and global Sass/CSS Modules support.

historical_context.label: Next.js 9.5 — July 2020
historical_context.description: Incremental Static Regeneration, rewrites and redirects.

historical_context.label: Next.js 11 — June 2021
historical_context.description: Webpack 5, Next.js Live preview and experimental CRA migration.

historical_context.label: Next.js 12 — October 2021
historical_context.description: Rust compiler, AVIF, Edge Functions, Middleware, native ESM and URL imports.

historical_context.label: Next.js 13 — October 2022
historical_context.description: App Router beta, layouts, React Server Components, streaming, new data-fetching methods, Turbo toolchain.

historical_context.label: Next.js 13.4 — May 2023
historical_context.description: App Router became stable for production use.

historical_context.label: Next.js 14 — October 2023
historical_context.description: Source attributes improved memory management using edge runtime.

historical_context.label: Next.js 15 — October 2024
historical_context.description: Rust-based Turbopack, React 19 support and asynchronous request APIs.
